title: VPC escape-hatch: passive fallback and observed rollback playbook for data-plane rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a defensive "escape-hatch" mechanism and an "observed rollback" playbook for Private (VPC) data-plane runtime upgrades. The goal is zero-downtime upgrades for customer VPCs while enabling an automated passive fallback to the previous runtime variant when production metrics indicate regression. This ticket covers Terraform module changes, canary gating hooks, synthetic probing, automated drift detection, and an operator-visible abort/escape path.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes 'escape_hatch' boolean and 'fallback_version' module variable
Upgrade pipeline can mark a rollout 'passive' which preserves old runtime pods and configures weighted routing without immediate termination
Synthetic probe suite (prometheus blackbox + loadgen) runs against every canary slice and feeds metrics to rollback detector
Rollback detector can flip router weights to 100% previous runtime within 30s of threshold breach without user intervention
Manual abort flow shows single-click 'evacuate-to-previous' in console with audit log entry and Terraform plan link
Runbook tested in staging by performing a controlled regression and triggering an automated observed rollback
tasks: Design Terraform variable schema and module outputs for escape_hatch (ashap/tf-vpc-deploy#42)
Add router-weight controller hook to set passive weights and preserve old runtime replicas
Implement 'rollback-detector' service using Prometheus rules + small webhook to routing controller
Add synthetic probe suite and integrate with existing synthetic-monitoring dashboards
Author console UI affordance for 'escape hatch' and single-click rollback with audit metadata
Write operator runbook and automation tests; run CHAOS test in staging cluster
tests: Unit: terraform plan/apply simulation with escape_hatch=true and fallback_version pinned
Integration: staging rollout with injected latency regression and automated observed rollback should revert weights
E2E: console button triggers Terraform apply that restores previous module outputs and validator passes
Chaos: kill 30% new-pipeline replicas during passive rollout and verify no customer-impact metrics spike beyond threshold
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Module landing - merge TF variable change and keep default escape_hatch=false
Stage 2: Router hook - implement weighted routing controller with passive mode (no immediate pod termination)
Stage 3: Observability - synthetic probes + Prometheus rules + Grafana dashboard panels
Stage 4: Automation - rollback-detector webhook + Terraform plan artifact publishing
Stage 5: Staging validation - execute controlled regression tests; runbook dry-run
Stage 6: Canary pilot - enable escape_hatch on 5 internal VPCs for 2 weeks
Stage 7: Ramp - opt-in customers; monitor and iterate; flip default to 'true' only after 4 successful pilots
rollback_playbook: Trigger detection: rollback-detector fires when two of three signals breach thresholds: request_error_rate, p95_latency, model_output_regression_score
Immediate action: routing controller executes 'passive-degrade' which moves 100% weight to fallback_version while leaving new pods in standby state
Short-circuit: publish Terraform plan that reverts module version pin and apply state; capture plan URL in console event
Operator notification: send PagerDuty with runbook link and provide single-click console button to approve a full state re-apply
Post-rollback validation: run focused synthetic tests (smoke + 1k sample traces) and require green before marking rollout canceled
Postmortem: create incident doc, attach telemetry, and schedule a remediation ticket for root cause
monitoring_thresholds: request_error_rate: >0.5% delta relative to baseline over 3m
p95_latency: absolute > 800ms or +40% relative to baseline over 3m
model_output_regression_score: automated eval drop > 2.5% on QA prompt set
risk: New passive fallback increases surface area for stale KV/cache divergence between old and new runtime. If not gated, failback could surface correctness regressions. There is also terraform state drift risk if escape_hatch toggles are not coordinated with controller state.
mitigation: Include cache-reconcile step in rollback-detector before moving live traffic
Add preflight check in Terraform plan to ensure module state aligns with routing-controller observed state
Constrain escape_hatch deploys to tenant-slice namespaces for first two pilots
Require security review on any module that exposes fallback_version to ensure no secrets or IAM escalation
notes: Design decision: passive fallback chosen over active immediate swap because it allows faster rollback without forcing heavy snapshotting
We punted on fully automating KV rehydration; instead we will surface a cache-reconcile task in the runbook to be executed during rollback
This ticket intentionally leaves 'automatic full-revert of Terraform state' as opt-in via operator approval due to blast-radius concerns
